Algorithm 5 ExtrapolatedHalpern, p.20; Sections 6–8 pp.18–23. Fixed eta, projected extrapolated warm starts, actual final approximate proximal point/normal, and saved G-to-F value recovery are covered. Definition 5.1 p.16, (8.2) p.22 and Section 9 p.24 require every active ancestor cap to be charged before each descendant original query, with immediate interruption.

Algorithm 6 HigherOrderVI, p.25; finite hierarchy proof pp.23–24 and Corollary 9.1 p.24. Appendix A.1 p.34 supplies known affine-hull tensor projection and normal lift with no accuracy or oracle-order loss; this is a covered algorithm component, not a claim of a separate published affine-hull Theorem.

Flat-gated chain: Section 10 pp.25–27, (10.1)–(10.7), with deterministic resisting realization Theorem 11.1 p.28 and fixed-random-frame randomized realization Theorem 11.3 pp.29–30; normalization continues pp.30–31. Construction, model membership, full-jet hiding, information-to-residual bridge, both realizations and dimensional/feasible-query restrictions are covered by the fixed records below.

Independent opposite-constant family: Lemma 11.5 p.30, normalization context pp.30–31. Disjoint endpoint success sets prove zero-query necessity; this pair supplies no positive-budget power-law hardness.

necessary_context.content: Finite-dimensional Euclidean spaces; known nonempty compact convex X with diam(X)<=D and x0 in X. F is C^(p-1) on a neighborhood, monotone on X, and Lip(D^(p-1)F)<=Lp in multilinear operator norm. N_X(x)={n:<n,z-x><=0 for every z in X}; r_tan(x)=inf_n ||F(x)+n|| over this outward normal cone.

Adaptive measurable query/output rules are defined and feasible on every transcript, with independent algorithm seed. All original-F calls count under a worst-case cap. Exact computations involving the known domain and returned Taylor coefficients are internal operations; an unknown-F resolvent is not free.
